transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Yeah, nice to meet you too. So, what brings me in... I guess it's mostly work stuff. I'm a construction manager, and lately, well, like if I start a safety briefing for the guys, or I sit down to do a plan review, I go into it trying really hard to pay attention, right? But within minutes, my mind is just off on three other job problems. 

Like yesterday, I was supposed to be looking at the framing specs, and suddenly I'm thinking about the lumber delivery. Which actually reminds me, the supplier changed their delivery route and now they're trying to bring those massive flat
Did you have these same kinds of trouble paying attention when you were a kid?

Yeah, actually. I mean, back in elementary school, my teachers were already telling my parents I couldn't stay in my seat. I talked out of turn, lost my homework, rushed through directions before I even really understood them... which, you know, my mom used to keep all my old report cards in this big blue binder. She was super organized like that. Had a label maker and everything. I actually bought a label maker last year thinking it would help me sort out my truck, because the cab is just a disaster zone of blueprints and fast food wrappers. But I think I lost the label maker. Or maybe it's under the passenger seat. I should probably clean that out this weekend before it gets too hot out.
Have these focus problems been causing trouble for you at work?
Yeah, it really is. It’s gotten bad enough that my boss actually pulled me in recently for a formal sit-down about it. Just because I keep missing follow-ups, and my site
Do these focus problems also happen outside of work?

Yeah, they definitely do. At home, it's... well, my wife is just completely worn down by it. Like, I'll tell her I'm gonna handle something, you know, fix the leaky faucet in the guest bath or call the insurance guy, and I mean to do it, I really do. But then I just... don't. Or I forget. And she has to remind me over and over. Which is funny, because her dad was a plumber, so you'd think she could just fix the faucet herself, right? He used to have this old Ford van, totally rusted out on the bottom, but he kept the inside immaculate. All his wrenches lined up by size. I always wanted to set up my truck like that. I even bought this modular shelving unit for the bed of the truck a few months ago, but it's still sitting in the boxes in the garage. Taking up half the space, actually. I really need to put that together. But yeah, she's pretty fed up with having to manage me on top of everything else.
When your mind drifts, is it usually because you’re worrying about things?

No, I wouldn't really say I'm worrying. It's not like I'm sitting there stressing out about things. It's more like... I'll be looking at a materials list for a job, and then I'll notice a fly buzzing near the window, and I start wondering how long flies actually live. Which usually makes me think about this documentary I saw about cicadas. You know they stay underground for like seventeen years? That's just crazy to me. Just sitting in the dirt for almost two decades. 

Actually, we hit a massive root system and a ton of grubs when we were excavating a foundation last week on the new subdivision over off Route 9. The backhoe operator, Jimmy, he's a good guy, but man, he is just rough on the equipment. He blew a hydraulic line on Tuesday and oil got absolutely everywhere.
